highlights.summary: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus has spent the last few days getting review-bombed on Steam after it was discovered that a particular segment of the game used AI music. Reddit user ShweetsStuff discovered the songs used during a Grand Theft Auto -themed section.
body: Creator Edmund McMillen claims he ‘had no idea’ AI music was used in the latest version of Binding of Isaac.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Creator Edmund McMillen took to X to apologize and claimed he “had no idea” the in-game GTA parody used generative AI music. Adding to the drama, Valve requires developers to disclose how and when they use generative AI in the development process, and Nicalis, Inc., the studio behind Repentance Plus, doesn’t appear to have mentioned the AI music anywhere.

Within hours of the discovery, Nicalis shared on X that Repentance Plus had been updated and the generated music files had been removed. While reviews on Steam have yet to rebound, and the game is still rated as “overwhelmingly negative,” users on X seem to be giving McMillen the benefit of the doubt, likely because he’s been quite outspoken on AI in game development, calling it “ uninspired and bland ” in a TikTok from 2024.

body: You Can See Everything continues visualizing box office success at a level that puts it in elite company as a documentary.

Over the weekend, You Can See Everything also became the first documentary film to have been watched by one million Letterboxd members. It becomes the 19th movie released in 2026 to join the “One Million Watched Club,” and with its 4.61 average Letterboxd rating, it is the second-highest-rated feature to hit the milestone, behind only 12 Angry Men with 4.63. You Can See Everything is the highest-rated 2026 film and the second-highest-rated documentary ever, trailing only Stop Making Sense on the social platform.

Among the box office achievements for You Can See Everything include opening with $15.6 million in its debut frame to register the second-biggest domestic launch for a non-music documentary, behind 2004’s Fahrenheit 9/11. The Holmes documentary also scored the highest-grossing domestic opening weekend for a release in fewer than 1,000 theaters since 2006’s Borat. You Can See Everything went on become the first documentary to reach No. 1 domestically in its third weekend of release.

highlights.title: When the Days of Being Wild Come to an End
highlights.summary: I used to romanticize being a bit of a disaster. Now, I have become a man who just...likes things to be nice.
body: This week, after reading up about the major differences between sea salt and rock salt, I found myself looking at a shot of my mates in an east London restaurant’s smoking area. My friends looked happy—mildly drunk, joyous, their night still full of possibility—and I felt… hmmm… hard to say what I felt. Not jealous, not one bit, but also not relieved that I was home and dry. Maybe the word is content? Happy enough for them without longing for a sip from the same goblet.

I rather romanticized being a bit of a disaster. I think we all did back then. Blame Pete Doherty. There was something appealing about running on…erm… adrenaline, partying at capacity, being slightly behind on everything else. I mistook a lack of self-preservation for spontaneity and great swathes of disorganization for having a social life. I didn’t want to become one of those people who had everything Filofaxed; those people had missed the point of being alive.

highlights.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
highlights.summary: Three significant backers share what gave them conviction to bet billions on Anthropic.
body: When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history.

But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year.
“We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch.

highlights.title: Robert Pattinson's Forgotten Dark Fantasy Thriller Proves He's a Perfect James Bond
highlights.summary: Not everybody is convinced Robert Pattinson is the right choice to be the next James Bond. Some are complaining Bond should be played by someone less famous, like he has in the past. Others feel he’s not masculine enough, or good-looking enough, or charismatic enough.
body: Honestly, I do think there is some merit to the idea that Bond should be played by an up-and-comer, if only because that’s been the tradition. (Clearly Amazon, which took over the franchise in 2025, has other ideas.) As for the more cosmetic complaints, I guess those all come down to personal taste.

As for the Twilight-related concerns, I understand them because, when Pattinson was announced as Batman back in 2019, I thought​​​​​​​ “Oh no, the Twilight guy? How could this guy, who seemed so… soft, be the Dark Knight?” I hated the idea. Then, a few months after the announcement, I saw the Robert Eggers film The Lighthouse and completely changed my mind.

The Lighthouse really is just about two guys in a lighthouse dealing with the loneliness of the job, which requires them to be stuck at sea for weeks at a time. Dafoe plays a grouchy old sea-dog, while Pattinson is his young apprentice. The movie is a laugh riot, with lots of drinking, some wild singing, and both men becoming increasingly unhinged. One dreams he has sex with a mermaid, the other masturbates all the time, and both are brought to their breaking point by the end.

highlights.title: An age gap isn’t always a problem, partner abuse is | Letters
highlights.summary: Readers respond to articles on relationships and the age of consent. Regarding Polly Hudson’s article ( At 17, I dated a 36-year-old. That decision looks very different to me now, 15 November ), I met and lived with a 35-year-old man when I was 17.
body: I learned that he had done it all before, pursuing schoolgirls. I tried to break free multiple times, only to find that he had phoned my new partner, or read my diary so he could block my plans. This is about having control, it is not just a sexual preference.

The men doing this are rarely satisfied, and criticism can escalate to coercive, emotionally abusive levels. In some cases (though not in mine) girls are pimped out, shared with the man’s friends, imprisoned against their will.

Polly Hudson should not be angry with her younger self. Would she be angry with another young girl who found herself in similar circumstances? Unlikely. There is something else that has stopped us speaking out: fear. Fear of physical or verbal retaliation by the perpetrator; of the judgment of those around us; of a legal system that fails to punish abusers and shames victims with hackneyed tropes that have long been disproven; of public and private organisations that continue to bury abuse allegations and enable perpetrators who bring in cash, clicks, viewers or shareholders.

body: Large language models can now redesign your TV and upgrade your camera for you. Is the physical world ready to be Claude Code-d?

Like so many things with AI, it’s not that large language models opened up some wholly new capability. For as long as there have been gadgets, a few users have been hacking, modding, jailbreaking, and tweaking them to their liking. What is new is that it’s easy now. People all over the world are discovering that they can use large language models to hack their hardware simply by prompting Claude Code or Codex to do it. It has led to a boom in developer-friendly gadgets and created a market for better software on just about every device you can think of.

highlights.title: 34 Years Later, the Best 'Far Side' Quote Will Still Leave You Speechless
highlights.summary: Larson didn’t do deep and inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful. Larson’s work was brilliant, and it sometimes took a few minutes to figure out what the punchline was.
body: In recent months, I’ve been examining the best-ever quotes from various newspaper comic strips, and in that time I’ve determined that every comic strip requires its own approach. For Charles Schulz’s Peanuts, I chose something heartfelt and inspirational because those comics and characters really have inspired people. For Bill Watterson’s Calvin and Hobbes, I investigated something more philosophical, as the best of those comics make the audience contemplate human nature and the world around them. But for Gary Larson’s The Far Side, the task is monumentally different.
Larson’s work often requires the reader to investigate something, but usually not in any kind of overly deep way.

The Far Side is brilliant, but it's not the kind of comic strip that makes you ponder life’s big questions. Larson channeled his genius into joke-telling, and that’s what made The Far Side so sharply funny. As such, determining Larson’s best-ever Far Side quote shouldn’t be some insightful, inspirational, or thoughtful journey — even though I did try going that way at first.

Larson’s work was brilliant, and it sometimes took a few minutes to figure out what the punchline was.

highlights.title: The link between nurturing and masculinity | Letter
highlights.summary: Clincal psychotherapist Gareth Strangemore-Jones responds to an article on persistent assumptions about masculinity. Sarah Blaffer Hrdy’s research offers an important challenge to one of our most persistent assumptions about masculinity: that nurturing is somehow contrary to male nature ( Would…
body: We often imagine psychological development as a process in which attitudes must change before behaviour follows. Yet caregiving may work in both directions. Repeated experiences of responding to another person’s vulnerability can engage and potentially strengthen the biological and psychological systems involved in emotional responsiveness, attachment and cooperation.

But we should be cautious about extending this into the claim that more nurturing fathers would necessarily produce a more peaceful world. Human beings are capable of extraordinary tenderness towards their own children while remaining hostile towards those outside their immediate circle. Empathy can be selective, and the causes of collective violence extend far beyond individual temperament.
Perhaps the more important question is whether the emotional capacities developed through caregiving can be extended towards strangers, communities and people with whom we disagree.

highlights.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
highlights.summary: To establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how to measure speed.
body: A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity.

Slowing AI development became a particularly hot topic after a former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher said the companies were “gambling with our lives,” and even Anthropic’s IPO filing suggested that the technology could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to society.”

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei then published a plan to “pace the frontier,” seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Among other things, Amodei called for companies to agree to “common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.”

In Pachochki’s argument, benchmarks that focus on AI’s “downstream capabilities” have quickly become outdated as the technology advances. But perplexity — which “measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions” — has remained “informative.”

That's not the only Star Wars release getting the deluxe IMAX treatment next year. highlights.title: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent
highlights.summary: Major US financial institutions are banning third-party bots from logging into your accounts—and warning that any costly bot mistakes are strictly your problem.
body: Wells Fargo is set to enact an updated agreement with millions of customers, specifically about AI agents, starting on Tuesday. The bank’s warning to early adopters could not be clearer. “Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK,” read Wells Fargo’s new terms.

AI agents, which automate online tasks and click on your behalf, have stumbled through 2026. They remain nascent technology, but a growing subset of power users latched onto the personal bots this year. Sometimes these early adopters enjoyed the efficient help of automation, and other times they publicly embarrassed themselves when the AI agents made major mistakes, like posting bank details for everyone at work to see.

Builders of these AI tools often market agents as the ultimate tool for shopping decisions, whether that’s putting together a grocery order, finding accommodations for a vacation, or discovering specific holiday gifts for your parents. I’ve used an agent to help shop for a new couch, comparing options within a specific budget and tracking price drops.

highlights.title: Kate Bishop Actress Hailee Steinfeld Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday
highlights.summary: Marvel Studios has confirmed Kate Bishop actress Hailee Steinfeld as a last-minute addition to the cast of Avengers: Doomsday. Marvel Studios announced the surprise return of Hawkeye's Disney+ partner in a nonchalant Instagram reel tonight.
body: "Catch Hailee Steinfeld in Disney's Hexed before she returns in Avengers: Doomsday," the post said.

You'd be forgiven for thinking Steinfeld was already included in Doomsday's already enormous lineup of superheroes and A-listers. Everyone from Robert Downey Jr. and Pedro Pascal to Tom Hiddleston has previously been confirmed to make an appearance of some kind, but Steinfeld was one of a few names to have been curiously benched up until this point.

She first appeared as the bow-wielding Kate Bishop in the Jeremy Renner-led 2021 show, Hawkeye. Aside from a The Marvels cameo and some animated voice work, Steinfeld hasn't spent too much time in the Marvel Cinematic Universe as the multiverse saga has rolled on. That won't stop her from helping out in the first chapter of its finale, though.

With the cast already stacked, it's hard to know just how prominently her character will be featured amongst the chaos. Between the Avengers, the New Avengers, Fantastic Four, and X-Men, there will likely be little room to explore how she gets along with the rest of the crew. For many, just the fact that she'll help in the fight against Doctor Doom is probably enough.

highlights.title: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash
highlights.summary: Journalist Paris Marx unpacks his new book "Hyperscale."
body: In his new book “Hyperscale,” journalist Paris Marx investigates the impact of data centers and generative AI, taking readers inside the data centers themselves and explaining how computing infrastructure that goes back decades recently became a political landmine.

The book is well-timed, to put it mildly, as data center backlash seems to have been one of the motivators for the massive blue wave seen in the recent midterm elections. And those debates are likely to continue as Democrats wield more governmental power.

In an interview with TechCrunch, Marx described the data center buildout as “fundamentally unsustainable” and “completely out of line with a livable planet,” while also arguing that these facilities make for an obvious target amidst broader anger at the tech industry. After all, if a data center is being built in your community, “it’s very physical, it’s very material.”

highlights.title: Mets reportedly agree $450m contract with Tarik Skubal, richest deal for pitcher in MLB history
highlights.summary: Ace’s contract reportedly for nine years. Mets have missed playoffs for last two seasons. The New York Mets look to have sealed the biggest deal of MLB’s offseason by signing free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal.
body: The New York Post’s Jon Heyman reported that the deal is worth $450m over nine years, the largest contract for a pitcher in baseball history. The previous record was for the $325m, 12-year deal Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers in 2024.

The left-hander, a two-time Cy Young winner, is one of the best pitchers in baseball. He turned 30 last week, and had surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow in May, but was still a prized target for teams looking to contend in the coming seasons. He ​reportedly also met with ​the Toronto Blue Jays, San Diego Padres and Los ​Angeles Dodgers.
Skubal’s agreement reportedly includes a full no-trade clause and a $45m signing bonus that is shielded from the management lockout that threatens the 2027 season.

Skubal is 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA in 88 starts over the last four seasons, striking out 655 and walking 95 in 546 innings. Over his seven-year major league career, Skubal is 66-44 with a 3.02 ERA. Skubal made his MLB debut for the Detroit Tigers and remained at the club until he was traded to the Dodgers this summer.

body: The Switch 2 only comes with 256GB of onboard storage and it will run out faster than you think. If you have a standard MicroSD card from your previous Switch, it won't work on the Switch 2. Although the two might look similar, the MicroSD Express card is much faster than its predecessor. The Samsung P9 model boasts transfer speeds of up to 800MB/s.

Quite a few games have now been released for the Switch 2 and some of them require an enormous amount of space. Final Fantasy 14 is the most gigabyte-hungry game to date, requiring about 117GB all by itself. That game alone takes up half of the Switch 2's internal storage capacity. Other plus-sized games include Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade (90GB), Split Fiction (70GB), Cyberpunk 2077 (60GB), and Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment (44GB). The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time tops out at about 27GB. Nowadays it's completely possible to download just three or four games and find yourself completely out of onboard storage.

highlights.title: Spain Pitches Incentives, Crews and a 500 Million-Strong Spanish-Speaking Market to India at WAVES Film Bazaar
highlights.summary: Spain, the Country of Honor at this year’s International Film Festival of India (IFFI), made its case to Indian filmmakers at WAVES Film Bazaar in Goa, laying out its incentives, locations and crews and pushing for closer co-production ties.
body: “For us, co-production is a key instrument,” said Camilo Vázquez, deputy director of the Institute of Cinematography and Audiovisual Arts (ICAA), the film agency of Spain’s Ministry of Culture. He pointed to better financing, exchanges between technical and artistic teams, and stories that could connect with audiences in both countries, and described the timing as particularly favorable for India-Spain partnerships.

For Indian producers weighing Spain as a filming destination, the offer extends beyond its locations. Usha Jadhav, a National Award-winning actor and producer with Spanish company ACortes Films, highlighted the country’s track record with international productions, its range of landscapes and architecture, and skilled crews used to working on both big-budget and independent films. She also cited eight-hour shifts and quieter shooting environments as practical advantages, particularly for sync-sound productions.
Jadhav said the relationship should not be limited to service work, and made a case for collaborations that bring creative teams together across borders.

highlights.title: Bon Appétit Pick: HelloFresh Garlicky Shrimp Couscous Bowl
highlights.summary: A cheffy detail helps pack a simple dish with flavor.
body: Most nights I try to hit up an exercise class after work, which means when I finally get home in the evening I'm tired, hungry, and craving something full of nutrients. With 26 grams of protein and just 25 minutes of prep-and-cook time, HelloFresh's Garlicky Shrimp Couscous Bowl is a great solution for dinner.

This flavorful bowl reminds me of Dig Inn's glory days—only I can enjoy it without elbowing my way through midtown lunchtime mobs. Roasted broccoli and shrimp sautéed with lemon and plenty of garlic are spooned on top of large couscous pearls. Chili flakes add an extra kick.

You'll need to grab olive oil, butter, salt, and pepper from your own pantry; everything else is included in your delivery. The shrimp arrives fully cleaned and deveined, thank god. I love that a small pouch of veggie stock is included for cooking your couscous, a detail that many meal kits overlook.
